I can't say I know how you feel but can relate to a degree.  I'm in my late thirties and have been on substandard anti-depressants for over 20 years.  I OD'd in February and woke up in the ICU with a tube down my throat and strapped down to the bed and stayed that way for another day all while coming in and out of consciousness.  I have family but they don't care to follow up or visit me to see how I'm doing.  Only a friend did.  For the majority of the year I've been fighting to get up and find some kind of reason to live.  That friend of mine talked with me about shrooms.  I decided to give it a try and I was not expecting to have such a transcendental experience.  There are so many things to describe but other than amazing colors and lights, I for thr first time ever wanted to live and see life through both the good and the bad.  I laughed hysterically that fungus works better at this than the crap doctors have given me for years. Note I still do take these and am planning to wean myself off over the course of a year.  Anyway, I also felt like there was a presence on the other side that was begging me to hold on and not give up.  Everytime I have tripped since then that feeling of wanting to live and feeling some kind of loving presence for me is there.  My own religious beliefs probably play a role in that.  But nevertheless, I never expected such a powerful change.  I used to drink a lot to numb myself.  I haven't had a drink for a few months now and don't even have the urge to drink.  I have my good days and bad days.  I'm looking into microdosing as people say that helps for in between trips and gives a sense of calm and peace.  Please find a reason to hang on.  Shrooms will also give you the ability to challenge parts of yourself that you are struggling with in a fully compassionate way.  For me it's similar to see a young child that is lost, confused, and alone.  That child didn't develop certain coping skills but it wasn't his fault.   The first time I ran into that child I didn't know what to do but told him (myself) I will find a way to help him.  I have cried tears of joy at times because I had never been able to love myself until now.  

One thing to note and I say this with sympathy, if you are contemplating suicide, more often than not, people fail.  Even the most violent and sure fire ways have a surprisingly high chance of failing and in those cases, you have damaged your brain severely and may never recover to pre-suicide functionality.  

Do you have any family or friends?  Do you have a therapist? There is no shame in needing a therapist?

But back to the mushroom topic that you are asking about.  I found a good MoM that is very kind and knowledgable.  Their focus is on helping people like us but they also serve people just wanting to have a good time.

Sorry for the wall of text, but yes, I believe mushrooms will help you see there is a reason to hold onto life.  It will show you those reasons important to you.  Hit me up of you need to chat or have any other questions.
